clue.text: Case supporting idle property owner

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other one

parts.note: idle means not working, so free
a case is a holder, something that holds an item

explanation.surface: A lazy landlord propped up by a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts HOLDER below FREE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owns land or a building outright, rather than leasing it, is the title for that kind of proprietor.

clue.text: White rebel is obliged to guards

indicators.note: guards means surrounds, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: is obliged to means must
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: A white rebel feels duty-bound to stand guard.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade was the leader of a 15th-century English peasants' revolt, a crossword favourite for 'rebel'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dry white wine from the Loire valley, so a white in the wine-list sense.

clue.text: It's said capacious hanky's needed, if you're like this

definitions.text: hanky's needed, if you're like this

indicators.note: it's said means the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: capacious means roomy, with plenty of space

explanation.surface: A big handkerchief is advised for anyone in this state.
explanation.walkthrough: Some solvers dispute that the two words sound alike, but in many accents they do.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery eyes and a runny nose call for a handkerchief, which is the condition described.

clue.text: Had a life before wife turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone had a life before a wife appeared on the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived' but signals that ERE W is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To have had a life is to have existed, the past plural of the verb to be.

clue.text: Confused detective hampered by gut reaction

indicators.note: hampered by means hemmed in by, so the detective sits inside the other word

parts.note: a gut reaction is an instinct
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A muddled detective is held back by trusting his gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blurred or unclear is not distinct, so confused in the sense of hazy.

clue.text: Cleric appearing on donkey in church causes deep division

indicators.note: in means placed inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: appearing on means sitting on top of, so the cleric comes first in this down entry

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A vicar riding a donkey into church causes a deep rift in the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep crack in a glacier is a dramatic example of a deep division.

clue.text: I stray off course in South American mountains

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other letters

parts.note: S and A abbreviate South and American
to err is to stray from the right course

explanation.surface: A traveller wanders lost in the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off course' tempts an anagram of I STRAY; it is part of the definition of ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a range of jagged mountains, a Spanish word used in South America.

clue.text: So close, having swopped ends

indicators.note: having swopped ends means the first and last letters change places

parts.note: to close is to shut

explanation.surface: Something nearly achieved, with its ends exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the S and T at the ends of SHUT.
explanation.definitionFit: So and the other word are both adverbs meaning in this way or therefore.

clue.text: Cut, but not polished, when suggested?

parts.note: rough means unfinished, not polished

indicators.note: suggested hints at a rough arrangement of the word when, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Something cut but left unpolished, as a rough draft is merely suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: HEWN is WHEN rearranged; the question mark flags the loose anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber or stone that is roughly chopped into shape has been cut without finishing.

clue.text: English invading prosperous foreign state

indicators.note: invading means entering, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: prosperous means rich

explanation.surface: England invading a wealthy country overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for empire or realm, used for the German state.

clue.text: 10 caught during escape don't count

indicators.note: during means within, so the letters go inside

parts.note: to elude is to escape
X is the Roman numeral for ten
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that seems to point at 10's answer, inside an escape scene.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to 10 across, but it is simply the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out of a reckoning is to not count it.

clue.text: Keels over, having striven in conflict

indicators.note: in conflict means in turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A combatant collapses after a hard struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to turn upside down, as a capsized boat does.

clue.text: Remarkably old theologian disheartened laity

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, keeping only the outside letters

explanation.surface: An elderly theologian has discouraged the lay congregation, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe something done in a strange or unusual way.

clue.text: Brave comic ultimately loses interest in script

parts.note: a wit is a comic person

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: hand means handwriting, a script

indicators.note: the word interest loses all but its final pair of letters, keeping only its end

explanation.surface: A comedian finally grows bored with the screenplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' keeps only the closing pair of letters of 'interest'; 'Brave' is a verb, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave something is to face it boldly and resist it, a verb sense.

clue.text: After fancy exercises, band's sobbing quietly

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the exercises follow the fancy

parts.note: a whim is a passing fancy
PE is physical education, exercises
a ring is a band

explanation.surface: After some fancy workouts, a band member is quietly in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying with soft, broken sounds is weeping in a low, feeble way.

clue.text: Confirmed nickname for Edward, the ocean sailor?

parts.note: the deep sea is the ocean
Ted is a familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: A nickname for a seafaring Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: A sailor called Edward who sails the ocean might be known as 'Deep-sea Ted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A confirmed habit is firmly established, ingrained deep down.

clue.text: Recondite manoeuvres protecting two hospital departments in secure housing

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so the departments go inside
in here means the second copy of the department is also placed inside the rearranged word
manoeuvres means moves about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
two says the department ENT is used twice, ear, nose and throat
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: Obscure moves shield two hospital wards inside a secure facility.
explanation.walkthrough: The two departments are not side by side: the rearranged letters wrap each one separately, so the single word protecting does two jobs and in carries the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre where people are held in custody is a form of secure accommodation.

clue.text: Complex seminars not quite hitting the mark

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so the letters are tangled up

explanation.surface: Difficult seminars that fail to get their point across.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot that just fails to strike its target is a narrow failure.

clue.text: Charge imposed on a variety of basic commercial vehicles

indicators.note: imposed on means placed on top, so the charge comes first in this down entry

parts.note: a tax is a charge

indicators.note: a variety of means a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A levy imposed on a range of basic goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabs for hire are vehicles used in business, carrying paying passengers.

clue.text: What's put out for famous moggy, perhaps on Yorks coast?

indicators.note: on means following on after

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town on the Yorkshire coast
a moggy, a British word for a cat, is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Laying out a welcome for a celebrity cat at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town on England's north-east coast in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson carpet is rolled out to honour celebrities and dignitaries arriving.

clue.text: Particular Democrat isn't first to yield

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A specific Democrat refuses to be the first to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fussy or fastidious about things is one sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Bond's partner formerly occupying Students' Union

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: James Bond's former girlfriend has taken over the student union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007; it is a link or connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A connection or tie linking things together is a bond.

clue.text: Sergeant, say, getting up one day full of himself?

indicators.note: full of means filled with, so the reversed day holds the officer inside it
getting up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Mon is Monday, one day of the week
himself refers back to the sergeant, a non-commissioned officer, an NCO

explanation.surface: A self-important sergeant rising one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of himself' looks like vanity, but 'himself' is the sergeant, an NCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer, so 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Person striving to keep motorways in better condition

indicators.note: to keep means holding inside

parts.note: a trier is someone who keeps trying
M stands for motorway, so MM for motorways

explanation.surface: Someone trying to keep the motorways in good repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitter and neater, as in more trim, is a comparative of being in good shape.

clue.text: Son's leaving even now to work in field

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter is removed

parts.note: still means even now

explanation.surface: A son still leaves to labour in the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: To plough and cultivate land is the agricultural verb for working a field.

clue.text: Husband's lacking in flair — a cure-all's offered

indicators.note: lacking in means missing, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: panache means style or flair

explanation.surface: A dull husband is offered a remedy for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy claimed to cure every ill is a universal remedy.

clue.text: Course of action at entering pub?

indicators.note: entering means going inside

parts.note: PH is a public house, a pub

explanation.surface: Is going into the pub the right way forward?
explanation.definitionFit: A route or line of conduct someone follows is a way forward.

clue.text: Manufacturer of cars, many with posh interior

indicators.note: interior means inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: lots means many
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A carmaker whose many models have plush interiors.
explanation.definitionFit: A British sports car company, making it a car manufacturer.

clue.text: Tsar's necessary after turn of century and easily dealt with

indicators.note: after means following, so the currency comes second
turn of means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, a century
the necessary is slang for money, and the Russian currency is the rouble

explanation.surface: A tsar needs money after the century turns, and it's simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the necessary' is British slang for money; a Tsar's money is Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causing no bother at all is simple to handle.
